chunks: From him, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿUrwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

For the muwaddiḥah injury there are five camels; for the simḥāq, four camels; for the bāḍiʿah, three camels; for the maʾmūmah, thirty-three camels; for the jāʾifah, thirty-three camels; and for the munaqqilah, fifteen camels.

key_terms.السِّمْحَاقِ: a wound reaching the thin membrane over the bone
key_terms.الْإِبِلِ: camels, the unit of diya compensation in this context
key_terms.الْبَاضِعَةِ: a wound that cuts into the flesh
key_terms.الْجَائِفَةِ: a penetrating wound reaching an internal cavity
key_terms.الْمَأْمُومَةِ: a head injury reaching the membrane of the brain
key_terms.الْمُنَقِّلَةِ: an injury that displaces or moves a bone
key_terms.الْمُوضِحَةِ: a wound that exposes the bone

ai.seo_question: What are the prescribed diya amounts for different types of wounds in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states the prescribed diya compensations for specific categories of wounds and injuries. It is a fiqh text that quantifies legal compensation for bodily harm, especially wounds to the head and body, within the Islamic justice system.
